record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Are there any restrictions on the algebraic type of the penci ls Ax+λa? Which algebraic types can be realised by means of an appropriately chosen Lie algebra? A recent observation by I. Kozlov (see details in [38]) shows that som e restrictions do exist. Roughly speaking, Kozlov has obtained the answer for Lie algebras of pure J ordan and pure Kronecker type. The mixed case remains open because of possible non-trivial interac tion between Kronecker and Jordan blocks. To further develop these ideas, it would be interesting to study Pois son pencils generated by one quadratic and one linear brackets. Compatible brackets of this kind appear, in particular, in the theory of Poisson-Lie groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over C with Lie bracket [·,·], and let g* denote its dual space. For each x ∈ g*, define the skew-symmetric bilinear form A_x on g by A_x(ξ, η) = ⟨x, [ξ, η]⟩. For a fixed regular covector a ∈ g*, consider the one-parameter pencil of skew-symmetric bilinear forms

    P_{x,a}(λ) := A_x + λ A_a,   x ∈ g*, λ ∈ C.

By the Jordan–Kronecker theorem, for generic x the pencil P_{x,a} admits a canonical decomposition into Kronecker blocks (of certain odd sizes) and Jordan blocks (associated with eigenvalues λ_i, of certain sizes); the collection of these block sizes and eigenvalue data is called the algebraic type of the pencil. A Lie algebra g is said to be of pure Kronecker type if all blocks of the generic pencil are Kronecker, of pure Jordan type if all blocks are Jordan, and of mixed type otherwise.

(a) Determine the precise restrictions (if any) on the algebraic types of pencils A_x + λ A_a that can arise from a finite-dimensional Lie algebra. Equivalently, characterize which collections of Kronecker block sizes and Jordan block data (sizes plus eigenvalues) are realizable as the Jordan–Kronecker invariant of some finite-dimensional Lie algebra g (with a appropriately chosen).

(b) In particular, resolve the mixed case in which the pencil contains both Kronecker and Jordan blocks, including all possible non-trivial interactions between them.

(c) Develop the analogous theory for compatible Poisson pencils on a vector space generated by one quadratic Poisson bracket and one linear Poisson bracket (such as those arising on Poisson–Lie groups): describe the possible algebraic types of such pencils and which can be realized.
artifact.status_search_result: The pure Kronecker and pure Jordan cases have been substantially clarified through work on Jordan–Kronecker invariants of finite-dimensional Lie algebras (Bolsinov–Zhang, Izosimov, Kozlov), and recent algorithmic and structural results (including 2024–2025 preprints on computing JK invariants and on stratification of matrix pencils) further constrain realizable types. However, no complete classification of realizable algebraic types in the mixed Kronecker+Jordan case has appeared, and the quadratic-plus-linear (Poisson–Lie) variant remains largely unexplored. The problem is therefore still open.

status_evidence.title: Jordan–Kronecker invariants of finite-dimensional Lie algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational work defining JK invariants and treating Kronecker/Jordan types of the pencil A_x+λA_a.
status_evidence.claim: Framework and partial results for pure types exist but the general (mixed) classification is not provided.

status_evidence.title: New techniques for calculation of Jordan-Kronecker invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) techniques for computing JK invariants for Lie algebras and representations.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing active research; no full classification of realizable algebraic types yet.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm for determining Lie algebra types
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic determination of Lie algebra Kronecker/Jordan type; stratification of pencils restricts JK invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Restrictions exist but a complete characterization in the mixed case has not been established.
